group.net.title: .NET and C#
group.net.blurb: Where .NET came from, how it works inside, the C# language, async code and user interfaces.
group.gfx.title: 3D and graphics
group.gfx.blurb: 3D model formats from meshes to BIM, and Three.js — 3D right in the browser, from the first cube to shaders.
group.more.title: More
course.history.title: The history of .NET
course.history.blurb: From .NET Framework 1.0 to .NET 10: Mono and Unity, .NET Core, why .NET Standard 2.1 works in Unity but not in the Framework, and what Revit runs on today. Flip through the years and pick TargetFrameworks for Revit, Unity and .NET 10.
course.dotnet.title: .NET under the hood
course.dotnet.blurb: How C# code turns into a running program. For complete beginners and for people coming from another language.
course.csharp.title: Deeper C#
course.csharp.blurb: For people who already write C#: how a type is built and value types, members and library versioning, parameters, generics, interfaces, delegates and closures, strings and enums, exceptions, reflection, LINQ and its cost, Span and defensive copies, pattern matching and what is new in C# 12–14. Pick where clauses, catch the closure in a for loop, count Where calls and reorder switch arms.
course.review.title: Code review: find the bugs
course.review.blurb: Four real interview tasks: ModelManager, ClashService, TileLoader and ClashMarkers. First take each trap apart on its own — mutable structs, async void, deadlocks, races, leaked materials — then click the buggy lines yourself in the full listing at the end of each unit.
course.async.title: Async/await in depth
course.async.blurb: From “why async at all” to the state machine, SynchronizationContext, the .Result deadlock, async in Unity, tasks without await and synchronization down to the memory model. Move time forward, catch a deadlock and step through MoveNext.
course.memory.title: Memory in .NET
course.memory.blurb: From operating system pages to the phases of the garbage collector: virtual memory, reserve and commit, the stack and CPU caches, how the heap is laid out, allocations, GC modes and tools. Why a process has three different kinds of “used” and how an array of structs outruns an array of objects.
course.avalonia.title: Avalonia basics
course.avalonia.blurb: Cross-platform UI in C# and XAML for Windows, macOS, Linux and more. Resize Grid columns, pick panels, fix bindings that do not update the screen and choose style selectors.
course.formats3d.title: 3D formats
course.formats3d.blurb: Meshes, CAD, BIM and point clouds: how glTF differs from FBX, STEP from STL and IFC from GLB. Build a mesh by hand, tessellate a cylinder, find clashes and estimate the size of a scan.
course.three1.title: Three.js: beginner
course.three1.blurb: The first scene, the camera, objects and hierarchy, lights and shadows, textures and loading glTF. Every rig runs real Three.js: switch lines of code on, turn fov and far, move the Moon to the Earth and light up shadows.
course.three2.title: Three.js: intermediate
course.three2.blurb: Environment maps and HDR, PBR for real, glTF animations and AnimationMixer, clicking objects with Raycaster, InstancedMesh and counting draw calls, post-processing.
course.three3.title: Three.js: advanced
course.three3.blurb: Your own shaders (ShaderMaterial, GLSL), WebGPURenderer and the TSL language, render targets, GPU particles, physics and React Three Fiber.
course.unity.title: Unity for programmers
course.unity.blurb: The MonoBehaviour lifecycle, coroutines, physics and rendering.
course.algo.title: Algorithms
course.algo.blurb: Interview problem patterns in short lessons.
